label: A possible contingent-free past from possible begun coming-to-be
description: New non-transcription conditional support option for premise A3 of the modal spine to God's existence, from a strictly weaker premise than the founded version. In the accessible history the contingent individual x is present at t, and some moment m at or before t has nothing earlier. m differs from t, because x present at m would need an earlier moment of absence; so m is strictly before t. Any contingent concrete individual present at m would likewise need an earlier moment, so m is free of contingent concrete individuals. No frame condition, presence contract, inertness of emptiness, well-foundedness or causal relation is used. The single premise is OPEN and is a possibility claim. Unlike the founded version, it does not conflict with every possible populated history having continuous time with a beginning. Nothing is attributed to a source. No premise truth is established.

research_comparisons.conditions: None beyond the two statements themselves: possibleContingentFreePast derives the negation of the rival from the target.
research_comparisons.scope: Same History carrier, Concrete predicate, preorder of times, frame and selected world.
research_comparisons.coverage: The initial-state rival as encoded (no accessible contingent-free moment before a contingent-populated one); not every philosophical view called an initial-state view.
research_comparisons.exclusivity: Checked incompatibility, not exhaustiveness: both statements can fail together.
research_comparisons.next_step: The rival's holder must deny that begun coming-to-be is possible: every accessible history either contains no present contingent concrete thing, or has some contingent concrete thing that never came to be, or has no populated moment whose past has a minimal moment (a beginningless past at every populated moment). The second horn no longer includes continuous time with a beginning.
